comparison.interpretation: All issued tasks are primary. Conditional behavioral regressions are not a causal estimate of compaction loss. Common eligibility is selected by pre-behavior. Native pruning, durable/context contents and loss mechanism remain unknown without separate evidence. Short runs do not demonstrate long-duration reliability; no superiority inference from this development batch.

limitations: The original cohort and scores remain unchanged. Later fixes were not used by these paid arms.
Reported usage components include cache and are not invoice tokens or dollar cost. Limit stops are outcomes under this envelope, not proof of intrinsic impossibility.
Requested-summary rates reflect the assigned experimental schedule, not a natural compaction frequency. Active-hour rates and hidden context loss are unmeasured.
The common API guide and permissions are repeated at each turn; their unaided retention is not tested.
Partial-restart's original numeric-rate contract was underspecified. Fraction-string rejection is preserved and qualified, not retroactively promoted.
A fresh exact checkpoint is required to attribute unchanged reports to a new observation. A malformed/extended checkpoint leaves their freshness unknown.
Conditional regressions, unknown follow-ups, initially wrong work and never-established behavior are distinct. Repeated obligations are not independent experimental units.
This small single-model Windows development cohort does not establish ALG superiority, multi-hour reliability, causal loss from compaction, or Linux live-model equivalence.
